contentEn:
When a Burnaby dental clinic needed to reopen its doors, time was not just money — every closed day was a day without patient care and without revenue. Reno Stars took on a full commercial renovation in Burnaby and completed the entire buildout in seven days. This is exactly what that week looked like, what drove the cost, and what every dentist or healthcare operator in Metro Vancouver should know before signing a contractor agreement.

Planning a healthcare renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

Why Dental Clinic Renovations Are Different From Residential

Residential remodels happen around your life. Commercial medical fit-outs happen around your revenue. A dental clinic in Burnaby that cannot see patients for three weeks loses not just three weeks of income — it risks patient attrition, referral disruption, and insurance billing gaps that compound far beyond the closure period.

The clinic Reno Stars worked with needed to stay closed for as short a window as possible. That single constraint reshaped every decision: material selection, trade sequencing, labour scheduling, and storage logistics all had to serve speed without sacrificing the compliance standards a healthcare facility requires.

Before starting any commercial renovation in BC, healthcare operators should confirm their contractor holds valid commercial general liability insurance and that the scope has been reviewed against WorksafeBC requirements for healthcare-adjacent work. Electrical and plumbing in a clinical setting may trigger additional inspections from the City of Burnaby beyond the standard building permit.

The One-Week Renovation Scope

The scope for this Burnaby clinic covered every zone of the practice:

  • Reception and waiting area: new reception desk with integrated cable management and durable seamless surfacing
  • Three consultation rooms: reconfigured layout, fresh drywall, new LED lighting, and floor-to-ceiling storage cabinetry
  • Staff kitchenette: re-plumbed, new countertops, cabinet repainting, new fixtures
  • Admin workspace: rewired for multiple workstations, data cabling, and ergonomic lighting
  • Doctor's private office: dedicated electrical circuit, new flooring, fresh paint
  • All common-area corridor and transition zones repainted and recarpeted

The before-and-after contrast in the consultation rooms was particularly sharp: dated, paint-worn walls and misaligned plumbing gave way to crisp white shaker cabinetry, quartz desk surfaces, and a layout that separated patient flow from staff movement — an infection-control improvement that came as a free byproduct of the renovation.

Commercial Renovation Cost Per Square Foot in Metro Vancouver 2026

Cost estimates for dental clinic fit-outs in the Metro Vancouver area typically range from $150 to $400 per square foot, depending on the complexity of the clinical requirements, the age of the existing building, and the specification level of finishes chosen. The following table summarises the cost factors that most directly affect final price:

Cost FactorTypical RangeNotes for Dental Clinics
Demolition and abatement$8–$20 / sq ftOlder clinics may contain asbestos-containing floor tile; abatement adds cost and timeline
Electrical and data$15–$40 / sq ftMedical offices require dedicated circuits for equipment; more than standard commercial
Plumbing and medical gas$12–$30 / sq ftSuction lines, water filtration, and HVAC modifications for clinical use
Drywall and interior framing$8–$18 / sq ftCompliance-grade drywall may be required in procedure zones
Cabinetry and countertops$20–$55 / sq ftQuartz is standard in healthcare; solid surface or laminate reduces cost
Flooring$6–$18 / sq ftSeamless sheet vinyl or rubber flooring preferred in clinical zones

Permits and inspections$2,000–$8,000 flatCity of Burnaby commercial permit + health authority review where applicable

The Reno Stars project for this Burnaby dental clinic covered approximately 1,200 square feet of clinical space across a reception zone, three consultation rooms, a kitchenette, and an admin area. The compressed one-week timeline meant heavier use of daytime labour across multiple trades simultaneously — a cost factor that was more than offset by the business continuity savings of a shorter closure.

For a typical dental clinic renovation budget in Metro Vancouver in 2026, most operators should plan between $180,000 and $480,000 for a mid-specification full fit-out of a 1,000–1,500 sq ft practice. High-end finishes or scope expansions into sterilization rooms and X-ray zones push costs higher.

The Trade Sequencing That Made One Week Possible

The reason most contractors quote three to five weeks for a commercial clinic fit-out is not the volume of work — it is the sequential dependency between trades. Electricians wait for framers. Plumbers wait for electricians. Cabinet installers wait for painters. In a seven-day sprint, that sequencing collapses into a carefully choreographed parallel operation.

Reno Stars scheduled three crews working simultaneously across separate zones of the clinic: one crew on demolition and framing, one on electrical and data rough-in, one on plumbing and medical gas connections. The second phase overlapped — cabinet installation started while the final electrical trim was still in progress in adjacent rooms. Finishing work — paint, flooring, fixture installation — ran in the zones that were dry while other zones were still receiving mechanical work.

The critical path ran through the consultation rooms, which required the most mechanical work — plumbing for three sinks, electrical for overhead lights and x-ray equipment circuits, data cabling for three workstations. Completing that zone by end of day five left two days for finishing, cleaning, and final inspection prep.

Before and After: What Changed at This Burnaby Clinic

The transformation was visible in every zone. In the reception area, the existing desk was removed and replaced with a custom quartz-topped reception counter with integrated cable management — eliminating the visible wiring that had been a housekeeping complaint for years and improving the first impression for arriving patients.

The consultation rooms received the most substantial functional upgrade. Three rooms that previously shared a single inefficient layout were reconfigured to separate the patient chair zone from the clinician's charting desk and supply storage. Floor-to-ceiling shaker cabinets in each room provided secure storage for clinical supplies that had previously cluttered counter space.

The staff kitchenette was relocated, replumbed, and fitted with new cabinets, a quartz countertop, and a commercial-grade sink. Staff who had been using the patient bathroom kitchen facilities now have a dedicated, compliant break space.

Permits, Inspections, and Regulatory Considerations for BC Healthcare Renovations

Dental clinic renovations in BC require a City of Burnaby commercial building permit regardless of the scope. For facilities that will hold an operating theatre or sedation area, additional review by a certified medical equipment planner may be required before permit issuance. The College of Dental Surgeons of British Columbia does not require their own approval for a renovation permit, but any changes to the physical layout of a registered dental corporation's premises should be documented for future inspection.

Fire code compliance for a commercial healthcare occupancy is stricter than for a standard retail or office tenant improvement. Exit corridor widths, door hardware specifications, and fire separation ratings between the clinical zone and any shared building structure must all be addressed in the permit drawings. A contractor unfamiliar with BC fire code requirements for Group B occupancies — which include healthcare facilities — can cause costly revision at the inspection stage.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a dental clinic renovation cost in Metro Vancouver?

Most dental clinic fit-outs in Metro Vancouver in 2026 cost between $180,000 and $480,000 for a mid-specification 1,000–1,500 sq ft practice, depending on finishes, mechanical complexity, and permit fees. High-end builds with sterilization rooms or dedicated X-ray zones run higher. Demolition and abatement of older finishes can add $8–$20 per square foot on top of base costs.

How long does a dental clinic renovation take?

A standard commercial dental fit-out for a 1,000–1,500 sq ft clinic typically takes three to five weeks with conventional scheduling. A one-week accelerated buildout is possible when the contractor coordinates multiple trades in parallel across separate zones — it requires a contractor with both the labour depth and the project management systems to manage simultaneous crews without trade conflicts.

Do dental clinic renovations in BC require a building permit?

Yes. Any commercial tenant improvement in the City of Burnaby requires a commercial building permit. Additional review may be required for changes to plumbing layouts, dedicated electrical circuits for medical equipment, or any work in a building that shares structure with other tenancies. Your contractor should handle the permit application as part of their scope.

What makes commercial clinic renovations different from office or retail?

Healthcare occupancies are classified as Group B under the BC Building Code, which imposes stricter requirements for fire separation, door hardware, mechanical systems, and accessibility than standard commercial occupancies. Dental clinics also require clinical-grade plumbing, additional electrical circuits for diagnostic equipment, and in some cases enhanced ventilation specifications.

Can a dental clinic renovation be done in phases?

Yes, and in many cases phase planning is the practical answer for a clinic that cannot afford a full closure. Common phase approaches: treat the consultation rooms first, then reception, then staff areas. A skilled commercial contractor will sequence phases to maintain infection control barriers between the active construction zone and any operating clinical areas.

What should I look for when hiring a contractor for a healthcare renovation in BC?

Verify that your contractor holds commercial general liability insurance, has experience with City of Burnaby commercial permits, and can provide references from healthcare or dental clients. Ask specifically whether they have worked in a Group B occupancy before, and confirm that their electricians and plumbers hold valid BC trade tickets. A contractor who cannot clearly explain the fire code requirements for your occupancy class is not equipped for a clinical fit-out.

一周装修的施工范围

高贵林这间诊所的装修范围覆盖了诊所的每个区域：

  • 接待和候诊区：新接待台，集成线缆管理，耐用的无缝台面

  • 所有公共走廊和过渡区域重新粉刷和更换地毯

诊疗室的前后对比尤为明显：陈旧、漆面剥落的墙壁和错位的管道被洁白的新风橱柜、石英台面和优化后的布局所取代——患者动线与员工动线分开，这是装修带来的感染控制改善。

Reno Stars 为高贵林这间牙科诊所的装修覆盖了约 1,200 平方英尺的临床空间，包括接待区、三间诊疗室、一个厨房和行政区域。一周的压缩工期意味着多工种同时加大日间劳动力使用——这部分额外成本由缩短停业期的业务连续性节省所抵消。

2026 年大温哥华典型牙科诊所装修预算，中档规格 1,000–1,500 平方英尺诊所，大部分运营商应计划在 18 万至 48 万加元之间。高端饰面或扩展到消毒室和 X 光区的范围会推高成本。

使一周工期成为可能的施工顺序

大多数承包商对商业诊所装修报三到五周的原因不是工作量——而是工序之间的顺序依赖。水电工等待框架工。管道工等待电工。橱柜安装工等待油漆工。在七天的冲刺中，这种顺序被精心策划的并行操作所颠覆。

Reno Stars 安排了三个工队在诊所的不同区域同时工作：一个工队负责拆除和框架，一个负责电气和数据粗装，一个负责管道和医疗气体连接。第二阶段重叠进行——在相邻房间最终电气调试仍在进行时，橱柜安装已在进行中。油漆、地板，固定装置安装等精装工作在干燥区域进行，而其他区域仍在进行机械工作。

关键路径穿过诊疗室，那里需要最多的机械工作——三台洗手池的管道、三台以上设备的照明和 X 光设备电路的专用电路、三台工作站的数据电缆。在第五天结束时完成该区域，为精装、清洁和最终检查准备留出了两天时间。

改造在每个区域都清晰可见。在接待区，现有接待台被拆除，更换为定制石英接待台，集成线缆管理——消除了多年来一直存在的可见布线问题，改善了患者的初次印象。

诊疗室获得了最显著的功能升级。三间原本布局低效的房间被重新配置，将患者牙椅区与临床医生的记录台和耗材储存分开。每间房间的整面到顶雪松橱柜为临床耗材提供了安全储存空间，此前这些物资一直杂乱地堆放在台面上。

员工厨房被重新安置，重新布管，并配备了新橱柜、石英台面和商用级水槽。员工现在有了一个专用的合规休息空间，不再使用患者卫生间的厨房设施。

BC 省医疗装修的许可证、检查和监管注意事项

BC 省牙科诊所装修需要获得高贵林市商业建筑许可证，无论工程范围如何。对于将持有手术室或镇静区的设施，可能需要在许可证发放前由认证医疗设备规划师进行额外审查。BC 省牙科医生学院不要求装修许可自己的批准，但注册牙科诊所场所的任何布局变更都应记录在案以备将来检查。

商业医疗占用的消防合规比标准零售或办公室租户改善要求更严格。走廊宽度、门五金规格以及临床区与任何共享建筑结构之间的防火隔离等级都必须在许可证图纸中解决。不熟悉 BC 建筑规范对 B 类占用要求的承包商可能在检查阶段导致代价高昂的修订。

常见问题

大温哥华牙科诊所装修一般多少钱？

2026 年大温哥华地区中档规格 1,000–1,500 平方英尺牙科诊所装修，大多数装修费用在 18 万至 48 万加元之间，具体取决于饰面、机械复杂程度和许可证费用。带有消毒室或专用 X 光区的高端装修费用更高。旧饰面的拆除和治理每平方英尺额外增加 8 至 20 加元。

牙科诊所装修需要多长时间？

1,000–1,500 平方英尺诊所的标准商业装修通常需要三到五周。一周加速完成是可能的，当承包商能够在不同区域协调多个工种同时工作——这需要承包商具备足够的劳动力深度和项目管理能力来管理同时进行的工队而不产生工种冲突。

BC 省牙科诊所装修需要建筑许可证吗？

需要。高贵林市的任何商业租户改善都需要商业建筑许可证。管道布局变更、医疗设备专用电路或任何与共享建筑结构相连的工程可能需要额外审查。您的承包商应作为其工作范围的一部分处理许可证申请。

商业诊所装修与办公室或零售装修有何不同？

医疗机构被归类为 BC 建筑规范下的 B 类占用，对防火隔离、门五金、机械系统和无障碍要求比标准商业占用更严格。牙科诊所还需要临床级管道、诊断设备的额外电路，在某些情况下还需要增强通风规格。

牙科诊所装修可以分阶段进行吗？

可以，在许多情况下，阶段规划是诊所无法承受全面停业的实际答案。常见阶段方式：先处理诊疗室，然后接待区，然后员工区域。经验丰富的商业承包商将安排阶段顺序，以在活跃装修区域和任何运营临床区域之间保持感染控制隔离。

聘请 BC 省医疗装修承包商时应该注意什么？

验证您的承包商持有商业综合责任险，具有高贵林市商业许可证经验，并能提供医疗或牙科客户的参考资料。具体询问他们是否曾在 B 类占用中工作过，并确认他们的电工和水管工持有有效的 BC 行业证书。不能清楚解释您占用等级的消防规范要求的承包商不具备临床装修的能力。
